title: Microflow Playground — sketch for multi-model composition + cost preview
content:
Topline idea:

Build a lightweight interactive "Microflow Playground" — a dev-facing UI + quick simulation runner that lets engineers compose small multi-step inference flows (sequence of prompts, model switches, rerankings, and fallbacks), see an estimated cost/latency profile, and run a dry-run with synthetic traffic or small sample CTAs. The goal is to make trade-offs visible early (cost vs quality vs latency) and speed iteration on production routing/rollback policies.

Why this?
- Teams often prototype multi-step assistants (summarize -> extract -> rewrite -> finalize) and then discover ballooning token cost or tail latency.
- Currently we have pieces: routing presets, model catalog, cost telemetry in Console, but no quick way to prototype a flow end-to-end and compare alternatives.
- Low-friction experimentation reduces expensive live testing on customers and encourages smarter defaults.

Primary users:
- Product/ML engineers building multi-step assistant features
- Solutions engineers doing customer demos (show cost savings with alternative variants)
- Internal benchmarking folks who need quick A/B style model composition tests

Goals and non-goals:
- Goal: Let a user assemble 2–6 step microflows (each step = prompt template + model + optional transform) and get quick per-run cost/latency estimate plus qualitative markers (where quality loss is likely).
- Goal: Provide saveable presets and compare two flows side-by-side.
- Goal: Quick dry-run with sample input or small batch (10–200 cases) that runs through the serving runtime with safe sandboxing (no external side effects).
- Non-goal: Full-blown experiment platform (no large-scale traffic sharding or long-term stats retention).

Key concepts / components:
- Step: {name, prompt (template or file), model selection (catalog pick), max_tokens, temperature, tooling (call function/reranker/embedding)}
- Flow: ordered list of steps + metadata (timeout budget, routing policy, fallback rules)
- Cost estimator: approximate token counts per prompt template (using tokenization heuristic) + model per-token rate (from pricing table) + simple latency estimate (model baseline + per-token time)
- Sandbox runner: runs a flow against a small set of inputs using safe credentials / deduped logging and returns traces + model outputs + token breakdown
- Compare view: two flows side-by-side with delta on cost, median latency, and sample outputs aligned by step

User stories (rough):
- As an ML engineer, I want to prototype a 3-step helper (summarize -> extract -> generate) and see estimated cost per request so I can choose a cheaper model for extraction.
- As a product PM, I want to run 50 sample queries through two flows and review where outputs diverge to decide which fallback works best.
- As an SE on a demo call, I want a preset that shows a high-quality vs budget flow to convince customers of predictable fallback behavior.

Success metrics (for initial alpha):
- Time to create and run a microflow < 10 minutes (measured in onboarding tests)
- Engineers report flow-level cost estimate matches real run within +/-25% for common templates (post hoc check)
- 20 internal flows created in first 4 weeks, 5 unique users reuse saved presets

Acceptance criteria / MVP feature list:
- UI to create/save/edit a microflow (basic form-driven editor)
- Step types: LLM call (prompt), embedding lookup, reranker (call to model and simple scorer)
- Cost estimator visible per-flow with breakdown by step and by token-ish (approx token estimates)
- Run button that executes against a sample input list (up to 100) and returns outputs + token counts + timing
- Compare two flows with side-by-side sample outputs and aggregate metrics

Mock UI notes (informal):
- Top: flow title + flow-level budget/timeout slider
- Center: drag-reorder list of steps; each step collapsible with sample prompt, model dropdown, caps
- Right column: live cost/latency estimate and small histogram of run latency (from sandbox)
- Bottom: run log/trace; clickable step to view input/output + token breakdown

Backend requirements (sketch):
- New microflow runner service that composes individual inference calls; uses existing routing layer to select model variants; tags requests as sandbox/test to avoid affecting production quotas.
- Token estimator module pulled from SDK tokenizers (fast JS/Python wrapper) with safeties for template loops
- Lightweight sandbox credential that routes to a dedicated quota pool (prevent accidental charge spikes)

Experimentation plan:
- Phase 1 (internal alpha): limit to internal users with a feature flag; use 50 sample queries; manually review outputs for privacy issues
- Phase 2 (expanded alpha): add small partner customers (opt-in) and measure estimator accuracy vs real traffic; gather feedback on UX
- Phase 3 (beta): integrate with Console presets and allow exporting flow -> route config for canaries

Open questions / risks (TODOs):
- How to score "quality" automatically? Simple heuristics (length, embedding similarity to ground truth) or require human label? Likely human-in-loop for now.
- Billing: sandbox dry-runs still consume tokens — do we bill internal vs customer? Need guardrails and quotas.
- Security: stored prompt templates may contain PII in examples — need redaction guidance and storage classification.
- Complexity: support too many step types will kill the UX. Start narrow: prompt calls + rerank + embed lookup.

Quick implementation sketch (approx):
- Frontend: React component reusing existing template editor, model selector, and Console cost table
- Backend: new /microflow/run endpoint that accepts flow + inputs, returns step traces; implement as orchestrator using existing inference API with sandbox flag
- Persistence: save flows as small JSON blobs in user namespace (no ML model artifacts)

Next steps (for me):
- [ ] Sync with Kai to get a quick prototype of cost estimator (Jira DEX-789)
- [ ] Draft minimal wireframes with Sam for dev handoff
- [ ] Create small GH repo skeleton and open PR for microflow-runner basic scaffold
- [ ] Add a security checklist item for prompt storage and sandbox quotas

Notes to self:
- Keep scope small. The biggest value is getting instant, comparable estimates; fancy auto-quality scoring can be added later.
- Demo idea: show the same user story with (a) single powerful model, (b) staged cheaper models with reranker, (c) cheap baseline + human fallback. Make cost/latency deltas obvious in the UI.

References / links to existing stuff:
- CONFLUENCE-1234 (routing presets research)
- JIRA-DEX-789 (estimator spike)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/microflow-playground/pull/12 (starter repo)

Random brainstorm fragments (untidy) :
- allow step-level ‘simulate worst-case tokens’ toggle
- show amortized cost per user-week (if we know typical session length)
- quick-export to route config (so a flow becomes a canary policy)

End of scratchpad.
